transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-10-23 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Diego/ Priya (Redwood SEs), Liam (CTO), Sofia (Head Infra), Noah (Security Eng)

Summary: quick intake to map MarinerForm's gating criteria before we scope a pilot. They are evaluating whether to use Redwood Hosted for speed or move to Dedicated/Private for keys and retention constraints.

00:00 Liam Chen: okay, thanks everyone for jumping on. we wanted to run through our security gating - we have a couple of product flows that touch customer PII so this is... important.
00:18 Ava Hartman: great, thanks Liam. quick intros — I'm Ava, AE at Redwood, Diego and Priya from our SE team will cover technicals. can you give us the most pressing controls you're worried about?
00:30 Noah Patel: sure, the big ones are: how do you handle keys (like KMS/HSM), audit logs and retention windows, SSO for our engineers via SAML, and RBAC so we can limit which services can call which models.
00:45 Diego Ramos: yep, totally. quick callout — Redwood has Hosted, Dedicated and Private options. Hosted is fastest to get started, Dedicated gives reserved GPUs and better isolation, Private gives you a customer-managed control plane and can be put inside VPCs or on-prem.
01:05 Sofia Alvarez: when you say private control plane, do we get to hold the keys, or is that still Redwood-managed? that's the major question.
01:18 Priya Shah: good Q. for Private we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations — you can bring your own key to the appliance or cloud wrapper. for Dedicated, we have KMS integrations but there are different ops models — with Dedicated we can offer envelope encryption where your master key lives in your KMS and we only get wrapped keys.
01:40 Noah Patel: so, in practice that means our master keys never leave our KMS?
01:45 Priya Shah: correct, master keys stay in your KMS/HSM. we store wrapped keys and rotate per our policy, but we can do key rotation tied to your schedule.
02:00 Liam Chen: how about audit logs — we need full request/response metadata for compliance, but we cannot retain raw PII payloads beyond 30 days. can you redact or obfuscate?
02:15 Diego Ramos: we do token-level and request-level logs; for Hosted we retain logs per tenancy and have configurable retention. we can support redaction rules at ingestion — e.g., mask based on regex patterns — but note that full redaction can impact forensic debugging.
02:35 Sofia Alvarez: are those logs exportable to our SIEM? we run Splunk.
02:40 Priya Shah: yes, logs can be exported to S3/Cloud Storage or streamed to syslog/forwarders; Splunk ingestion is common. retention can be set per-customer; we can also provide a push of archived logs periodically.
03:00 Noah Patel: what's your stance on SOC2 and ISO? do you have artifacts we can consume?
03:08 Ava Hartman: Redwood is SOC2 Type II compliant — we can provide the SOC2 summary and a redacted Type II report under NDA. ISO27001 is in progress in some regions — i can share our compliance deck.
03:30 Liam Chen: timeline: we need to close infra decisions by mid-November and start a POC in early December if possible.
03:40 Ava Hartman: that lines up — next steps we typically do: share SOC2 artifacts, propose Dedicated node sizing for their expected throughput, and run a 1-week POC where we clock latency and cost on a representative prompt set.
03:55 Diego Ramos: quick technical note — for low-latency routing we can pin requests to a Dedicated pool with KV cache warm-up. that reduces per-token cost and latency but requires prewarming for burst patterns.
04:10 Sofia Alvarez: can you talk through RBAC — particularly around token scoping, service accounts, and developer sandboxing? we want least-privilege so devs can't accidentally call the production models.
04:22 Priya Shah: absolutely. we have token scoping where tokens can be scoped by route, model, or quota. plus RBAC roles for Console access (Admin, Operator, Observer). for greater separation we recommend isolated Dedicated pools per environment (dev/stage/prod) tied to network controls.
04:45 Noah Patel: do you support SCIM provisioning from our IdP? we use Okta.
04:50 Diego Ramos: yes, SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning users and groups. we can map IdP groups to Console roles. some fields in SCIM are vendor-mapped so we usually test in a staging tenant.
05:05 Liam Chen: encryption — rest and transit?
05:08 Priya Shah: TLS in transit; at rest we use AES-256. for Hosted, keys are Redwood-managed by default but can be BYOK via cloud KMS. for Private deployments we can mount your HSM/KMS directly. there is also support for customer-supplied HSM on premises in air-gapped scenarios.
05:30 Sofia Alvarez: retention policy again — we cannot keep raw user prompts for more than 30 days. are there controls to auto-delete or keep obfuscated indexes?
05:40 Diego Ramos: yes, configurable retention policies. we also have prefix/KV caching for fast responses, and caches can be ephemeral or persisted depending on policy. if you enable auto-delete after X days we will scrub raw inputs; derivatives like embeddings may be treated separately and we can configure lifecycle rules.
06:05 Noah Patel: okay, two follow-ups: does Redwood have an audit trail that shows who rotated keys or who modified RBAC roles? we need that for audits.
06:15 Priya Shah: yes, admin audit logs track Console actions (role changes, key rotations, policy updates) with actor and timestamp. for Dedicated/Private we can also forward admin logs to your logging backend.
06:30 Liam Chen: competitor question — we tested an in-house setup last year; cost was crazy and ops overhead was heavy. if we go Dedicated with Redwood, can you give estimates for committed nodes vs burst?
06:45 Diego Ramos: we can, we'll draft sizing based on your traffic numbers. for committed Dedicated we offer baseline throughput and burst pools for spikes — cost model is a combination of reserved capacity + per-token compute for burst. we'll provide a proforma.
07:05 Sofia Alvarez: anything about data residency? we have EEA customers and need data not to leave eu region.
07:15 Ava Hartman: we have region-aware routing and hosting; for Hosted we have EU regions and can configure regional tenancy. for Private you can deploy in your cloud region or on-prem. we'll flag geo-residency as a requirement in the POC scope.
07:35 Noah Patel: can you support an aggressive retention audit — e.g., we want proof that data older than 30 days is purged and can't be recovered?
07:45 Priya Shah: we can provide a purge workflow and attestations. in Private/Dedicated we can run a verification job or produce logs showing deletion ops. for Hosted we provide deletion confirmations and deletion audit records, though some backups may have longer retention windows; we can discuss backup retention exceptions.
08:10 Liam Chen: ok great. let's talk about the POC prompts — we have three main vectors: customer support chat (PII), payment reconciliation (sensitive financial), and internal code-assistance (internal keys). we'd like a perf benchmark on those.
08:30 Diego Ramos: perfect — if you can provide obfuscated prompt sets and expected qps/peak, we'll run latency/throughput tests on both Hosted and Dedicated to show the deltas.
08:45 Sofia Alvarez: curious — are there differences in model catalogue between Hosted and Dedicated? some of the proprietary quantized models you advertise — are they available in Dedicated?
08:55 Priya Shah: most of the models in our catalog are available across modes; some specialty optimizations (e.g., AVX kernel tuning, quantized variants) are region/hardware dependent. we'll include compatibility notes in the sizing doc.
09:10 Noah Patel: one more nit — for RBAC: can we have service-to-service auth that prevents exfil via developer tokens? like short-lived service tokens and blocked console copy?
09:25 Diego Ramos: yes, we recommend short-lived service tokens and rotate them. console UI access is separate; we can disable token creation for certain roles and require approval flows.
09:35 Ava Hartman: great — time check, we're at ~50 minutes. quick recap and next steps?
09:40 Liam Chen: yes please.
09:43 Ava Hartman: recap: 1) Redwood to send SOC2 summary + redacted Type II report under NDA; 2) Redwood SEs to produce Dedicated sizing, regionized hosting options, and cost proforma; 3) MarinerForm to provide obfuscated prompt corpus and retention policy + sample logs; 4) schedule a 1-week POC in early December to test latency, KV cache behavior and key integration.
09:58 Sofia Alvarez: can we get the SOC2 by end of week? that helps legal.
10:02 Ava Hartman: yes i'll push that today.
10:05 Noah Patel: we'll get the obfuscated data set and retention doc to you by next Tuesday.
10:10 Diego Ramos: I'll follow up with a sizing spreadsheet and questions about peak qps.
10:15 Liam Chen: perfect, thanks all.

Action items (in call): Ava to share SOC2 artifacts; Diego to send sizing + cost; MarinerForm to provide obfuscated logs/prompts; schedule POC.

End of transcript.
